I am 61 years old with no schooling and only this half-hectare plot that my family has always farmed. Here in Shinyanga, the rains come once a year and leave quickly, so I grow what survives—likely sorghum or cassava intercropped with cowpea—using the manure from our few goats because I cannot afford shop fertilizer. I keep my own seed from last season, and since I have no money for chemicals or hired help, I will weed it myself with the hoe as I have always done.
